description.p: An aarch64 build of Plex Media Player that runs the current Plex desktop web client. Playback uses mpv. Hardware decoding is used where the system provides it, through a stateful V4L2 decoder or VA-API. Decoding falls back to software for any stream the hardware cannot decode correctly, which on a device whose decoder emits only 8 bit frames includes 10 bit, HDR and Dolby Vision video.
The Plex web client is downloaded from Plex at install time as extra data and is covered by Plex's own terms.

ul.li: The app sends the client to the Plex sign-in page by itself when the client reports ready and no Plex account session appears within twenty seconds. A device whose session has lapsed otherwise sits on the Home screen with a loading spinner and nothing to act on.

An Online Media Sources item in the settings menu, which opens the Plex page of that name. Its Discover Source setting removes the Trending and Activity tabs from Home, which report an error on this client. It is a Plex account setting and applies to every Plex app the account signs in to.
The Sign in to Plex item appears only when the client has no Plex account session.
Hardware video decoding through the system's stateful V4L2 decoder, for H.264, HEVC and VP9 where the device provides one. On the Steam Frame this takes 8 bit video off the CPU.

The hardware decoder is offered only for streams it can emit correctly. 10 bit, HDR and Dolby Vision video decodes in software, because a decoder that emits only 8 bit frames decodes 10 bit video into 8 bit samples without reporting an error.
The settings cog is hidden while video is on screen.
The Flatpak takes --device=all, which is what gives the sandbox the /dev/video* decoder nodes. Flatpak has no narrower option for them.
The settings menu and the update prompt take all keyboard, gamepad and mouse input while they are open, so the Plex interface behind them no longer responds.
An update is no longer offered when the installed build is newer than the published release. The comparison uses the build's time of day as well as its date.
The provider list sends the storage feature only in its JSON form.
A settings menu inside the app, opened with F1 or the gamepad's Menu button.

Update checks, with a manual check, a choice of cadence and release notes. The check compares the installed build's commit against the one the update repository publishes, so a rebuilt release is detected.
A download folder setting, with an option to confirm each download.
Text size and high contrast settings for the app's own screens.
Update reports arriving during an install no longer replace the install in progress.
A skipped version is recorded by the build's commit rather than by release tag.
Release notes are reached from the settings menu instead of a keyboard shortcut.
The settings list has a scroll bar and scrolls smoothly from the gamepad.
